newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan gold jewellery imports thrive despite slump.
newsitem.headline: Japan gold jewellery imports thrive despite slump.

text.p: Jewellery makers from Hong Kong to Milan are enjoying solid business in Japan despite a general slump in the domestic market and the weaker yen, and industry sources expect the trend to continue for years to come.
Japan is set to import a record amount of gold jewellery this calendar year, and some sources say foreign makers could overtake their Japanese rivals on their home turf in the not too distant future.

"Japan's jewellery industry has reached an important turning point," said Itsuo Toshima, area manager for the Japan branch of the World Gold Council (WGC). "Japan's gold jewellery imports could hit a record high this year, while domestic jewellery output has slumped."

Japan's imports of gold jewellery hit a record 27 tonnes in 1995, up by more than one-fourth from the year before and accounting for about one-third of total jewellery demand, according to industry data.

Gold jewellery imports are poised to set a record again this year, since they have risen 1.5 percent in the first nine months of this year from the same period of 1995, the WGC said. The influx of foreign-made jewellery comes despite the fact that a recent fall in the yen means higher import prices.

These gains in jewellery imports, albeit slight, defy the slide in sales of gold jewellery in Japan in recent years. Industry sources are predicting gold jewellery demand this year will fall by at least 10 to 20 percent.
Italian jewellery has become particularly popular, accounting for 40 percent of Japan's gold jewellery imports in the first nine months of this year, the WGC said.

Classy foreign brands like Gucci and Cartier are enjoying a renaissance among young Japanese, reminiscent of the boom seen during the late 1980s "bubble economy" of soaring asset prices and conspicuous consumption.
"Despite the high prices, Italian gold jewellery benefits from its sophisticated designs," a bullion house official said.
Less expensive jewellery from Asian centres like Hong Kong and Bangkok is also finding eager buyers in Japan, industry sources said.
Growth in jewellery imports from Asia could partly be attributed to Japanese makers shifting production to overseas factories in an effort to reduce costs, industry sources said.
"The current trend of imported gold jewellery increasing and taking market share from domestic producers will continue for a while," said the bullion house official.
"I would not rule out the possibility of the volume of imported gold jewellery surpassing domestic jewellery production in the next several years," he said.
Some industry officials, however, expressed doubts over whether Japan's jewellery imports will continue to rise.

"Japan's jewellery market has basically been struggling due to poor sales. Even concerning imported jewellery, gold jewellery sales have lost momentum compared with last year. The yen's recent weakness against the dollar could slow jewellery imports," an official at a jewelley maker said. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7431
